description.narrative: The number of people who will benefit from access to safe water, safe sanitation options and hygiene promotion is derived from the households affected by the cholera crisis. The targeted communities in the 4 wards (16,17, 19 and 33) all have farming compounds and an urban location called Glendale with a total of 5438 households broken down as follows; Mazoe Flowers (326hh), Panashe estate (86hh), Kachere estate (87hh), Mazoe citrus (231hh), Harmony (89hh), Duncombe (92hh) and Glendale town (4437hh), all translating to a total of 32 206 people when one household has an average size of 5 people according to the census results of 2022. The four wards above have already experienced cholera cases putting them at high risk of cholera spread.

The project aims to reduce cholera case load and mortality thus preventing and controlling local transmission. This is to be achieved through successful distribution of the hygiene enabling kits to the affected households and neighbors ensuring the Case Area Targeted Interventions approach is followed. Capacity building of Village Health Workers and Volunteers in conducting door-to-door hygiene promotion and reaching at least 80% of the targeted households with key Health and Hygiene messages aimed at creating communities that are resilient and responsive to future outbreaks of similar nature. This will also help to build better understanding on health and hygiene issues leading to improved good hygiene practices which is a key component of this response. Disaster Risk Reduction activities that include capacity building in all cholera response spheres will help to create a competent Rapid Response Team in the affected district and this will ensure enhanced future capacity to deal with potential outbreak.

The resurfacing of the cholera outbreak in Mazowe Flowers farm, a compound in Mazowe district, that started on the 19th of December 2024 came just less than 6 months after the country had been declared cholera free. By 06 January 2025, 10 culture confirmed cases and a cumulative total of 103 suspected cholera cases that included one fatality shows that the underlying causes of cholera have not been addressed decisively. Access to portable water is limited through rationing by the farmer as members fail to contribute towards water pumping of the motorized borehole by the responsible authority, leaving them with no option than to fetch the water from Mazowe River. The start fund is best suited to support interventions of such crisis due to the urgency with which the Network operates.
